status: contradicted by the extended empirical map; research record only
status_policy: The rule is an empirical regularity of the empirical map.  It predicts wrongly on a second protected corpus and is therefore never used to decode.

derivation.note: Every empirical key is reproduced; a byte seen at several positions yields one base.

independent_cross_check.note: The archived trace audit is not an independent proof of the Encoder format. The key 1:199 has no archived candidate at all, because the runtime trace of that file carries an extra instruction at that position; the rule therefore predicts it without contradicting the archive.

disputed_keys.note: The position rule reproduces 140 for these keys, but the native meaning of 140 stays unresolved; the Encoder level call semantics is handled by encoder_call_map.json.

limitations: The rule is fitted on the empirical map; it adds predictions, not new native observations.
Only bytes present in the byte base table can be predicted.
A negative prediction is refused instead of wrapped around.
The native semantics of a predicted opcode is not established by the rule itself.

measured_accuracy.note: The rule reproduces the empirical map exactly, but on a second protected corpus it predicted wrongly in 6 of 58 cases and the operand shape guard did not catch all of them.  The rule is therefore kept as a documented regularity of the map and is never used to decode an instruction the map does not contain.

contradiction_with_the_empirical_map.note: The rule was derived from the first 313 keys of the empirical map and reproduced all of them.  The map was later extended with 64 keys confirmed by a native trace of a second protected corpus, and four of the new keys contradict the rule.  The rule is therefore never used to decode an instruction the map does not contain.
